item.title: Pope Leo urges husbands to respect wives amid femicide crisis across Latin America
item.description:
Farmers face big drop in production from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event. High winds in parts of Colombia, one of the biggest suppliers to the UK market where droughts are predicted in some regions this year, and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body. In the Dominican Republic, farmers are expected to face drought conditions, with forecasts of drier and warmer than usual conditions. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourning in Poland after mass shooting
item.description:
Poland has launched a terrorism investigation after a deadly shooting left six people dead and 16 injured. The 24-year-old Polish suspect was reportedly fascinated by far-right ideologies. Authorities are investigating the possible extremist motive as Krakow's main square remains sealed. Two days of national mourning have been declared for the victims.

item.title: Week in politics: Democrats plan for the next Congress, Trump's new Chief of Staff
item.description:
President Donald Trump today announced that Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. That change does not bode well for anyone who hoped that Trump, chastened by his party's disastrous performance in the midterm elections, would moderate the policies that alienated voters. Truth Social Miller, previously a deputy chief of staff, is the main architect of Trump's immigration crackdown , which has targeted many peaceful and productive U.S. residents, contrary to the promise that it would focus on "the worst of the worst." Although Trump has intermittently expressed qualms about the impact of immigration enforcement on businesses and their longtime employees, Miller has made it clear that he favors an indiscriminate approach. item.title: South Africa’s ANC suffers setback in local elections
item.description:
Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted. Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party . Continue reading...

item.title: Pope’s visit to Argentina sets up showdown with ‘hyper-capitalist’ Milei
item.description:
A mototaxi drives past a banner of Pope Leo XIV in Chiclayo, Peru, on Nov. 5, 2026, ahead of his trip to Latin America. AP Photo/Martin Mejia Pope Leo XIV travels to Latin America on Nov. 6, 2026, with a packed itinerary that will bring him through Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It is Leo’s first trip to the region since his elevation to the papacy – and a homecoming for a pope who spent two decades in Peru and holds Peruvian citizenship. As a historian of Catholicism in the late 20th century , I couldn’t help but notice that the pope’s plans walk a fine line during a fraught political moment in Latin America. Leo plans to meet with the right-wing presidents of Argentina and Peru . He will also visit sites often associated with the progressive wing of the Catholic Church, including Casavalle, one of the poorest neighborhoods in Uruguay’s capital. item.title: Texas’ School Voucher Program Could Be “Unrecognizable, If Not Extinct,” Says Democratic Lawmaker
item.description:
Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa at a rally in Austin on Election Day. Leila Saidane for The Texas Tribune Texas Gov. Greg Abbott’s vision for education was finally coming together. This year, the state launched a voucher program that allowed roughly 110,000 of Texas’ more than 5 million schoolchildren to get a private education using taxpayer dollars. Abbott’s loyal appointee at the Texas Education Agency, Commissioner Mike Morath, was leading the state’s largest takeover of public schools in recent history . And the Texas State Board of Education, with Abbott’s support , helped pass a controversial new social studies curriculum that required teaching Bible stories and shifted away from world history to focus on Texas and the United States. item.title: Russell Brand to learn sentence after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault
item.description:
Russell Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court on Nov. 4, 2026 in London. Photo by Leon Neal/Getty Images. British comedian Russell Brand was found guilty of rape and sexual assault on Thursday. item.title: The American Dream Is No Match for Climate Change
item.description:
This story was originally published by Grist and is reproduced here as part of the Climate Desk collaboration. It is part of a series The Dream That Oil Built , which explores the connections between climate change, fossil fuels, and the American Dream. To Sierra Isley , the American Dream brings to mind a home ringed by a white picket fence. “The house in the suburbs is just what you’re taught growing up,” the 26-year-old said. “You know, that’s what you see on TV.” What she wanted for her life was a bit different from that picket-fence ideal, but she still saw the prospect of buying her first house two years ago as a chance to live out what she called “that big dream that everybody has as a kid.” Isley and her girlfriend, Jamie, were moving from Philadelphia to Asheville, North Carolina, and found a home they liked, a three-bedroom brick house with lots of natural light and a big tree…
